<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"

  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <groupId>com.example</groupId>
  <artifactId>app</artifactId>
  <version>0.1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>

  <properties>
    <maven.compiler.release>25</maven.compiler.release>
    <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>

    <slf4j.version>2.0.20</slf4j.version>

    <dependencies>
      <dependency>
        <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>

        <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
        <type>pom</type>
        <scope>import</scope>
      </dependency>
      <dependency>
        <groupId>org.junit</groupId>
        <artifactId>junit-bom</artifactId>
        <version>${junit.version}</version>
        <type>pom</type>
        <scope>import</scope>
      </dependency>
    </dependencies>
  </dependencyManagement>

  <dependencies>
    <!-- Logging facade: the only logging API application code compiles against. -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
      <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
    </dependency>

    <!--
      Logging backend. Runtime scope keeps Logback classes off the compile
      classpath, so code can't accidentally depend on it. Swap this for any

    <dependency>

      <artifactId>logback-classic</artifactId>

      <scope>runtime</scope>
    </dependency>

      <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3.16.0</version>

        <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>

        <version>3.6.4</version>

import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;

    public static void main(String[] args) {

        log.info(new Greeter().greet(args.length > 0 ? args[0] : "world"));
        log.info("Application finished");
    }
}
EOF

import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;

content.text:
I set up the project in `/work` using SLF4J as the logging facade and Logback as the backend. `mvn verify` passes (the one test passes), and `mvn exec:java` runs the app and logs through Logback.

**Layout**
```
pom.xml
.gitignore
src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java          – entry point, logs via SLF4J
src/main/java/com/example/app/Greeter.java      – example class with a debug log
src/main/resources/logback.xml                  – runtime config (app at INFO, everything else at WARN)
src/test/java/com/example/app/GreeterTest.java  – JUnit test
src/test/resources/logback-test.xml             – test config (app at DEBUG)
```

**How the code stays independent of the logging implementation**
- **`slf4j-api` 2.0.20** is the only logging library the code compiles against. Classes use `org.slf4j.Logger` and `LoggerFactory` only.
- **`logback-classic` 1.6.5** has `runtime` scope. Logback isn't on the compile classpath, so nobody can accidentally import its classes.
- **Switching backends** means changing that one dependency to another SLF4J backend, such as `slf4j-simple`, `log4j-slf4j2-impl` or `slf4j-jdk14`, and replacing `logback.xml`. No Java code changes.
- **Versions are managed centrally:** SLF4J and JUnit versions come from their BOMs (`slf4j-bom`, `junit-bom`). Versions are kept in properties.

**Other choices**
- The code targets Java 25, the current long-term support release; the installed JDK is 26.
- JUnit is 6.1.3.
- The plugins are pinned to the latest stable versions: compiler 3.16.0, surefire 3.6.0, exec 3.6.4.
- The group ID `com.example` and artifact ID `app` are placeholders. Rename them as needed.

**Common commands**
```
mvn verify                             # build and test
mvn exec:java -Dexec.args="YourName"   # run the app
```

I haven't committed anything. The `stderr.log` and `transcript.jsonl` files in the folder weren't created by me, and I left them alone.
